correctness.summary: Rooting at a maximum-degree vertex gives a sharp branch recurrence F_0=1 and F_i=1+ikF_{i-1}. Strong induction on branch order handles both upward and downward degree-class children; strict monotonicity of F_i makes every upward child strictly more expensive. The root bound and its equality conditions therefore force the unique layered extremizer. The degree-complexity-three spectrum follows independently from core edge and degree counts.

limitations: Complete theorem text of Das--Mishra--Rai (2023) was not inspected.
Complete theorem text of Adiyanyam et al. (2026) was not inspected.
Unindexed or differently phrased equivalent results remain possible.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The theorem specializes to the known k=1 minimum-order formula A392965. Full text of the 2024/2026 general k-SI extremal paper was checked and contains maximum-degree/size bounds and even-diameter results, not this tree minimum-order theorem. Searches across k-SI, 2-SI, prescribed maximum degree, minimum-order trees and degree-complexity formulations found no general-k equivalent. Two highly relevant papers were only available through abstracts/indexed descriptions and remain residual risks.

review_statement: Same-model review: passed. Independent audit: not yet performed.

value.summary: The result gives an exact minimum order for every admissible maximum degree and every k, uniquely characterizes the extremal tree, determines its radius and diameter, and yields an exact order spectrum for the first non-star degree-complexity class.
